terra.problem: Saying the boost was welcome attributes a feeling to Ezekiel without marking it as a guess.
The passage says they and their fathers rebelled, but does not say rebellion was passed down like a family habit.
The passage does not establish that the rebellion began before the exile.
The passage does not specify the number of years of rebellion, so it cannot rule out a few years.
The passage does not say whether the LORD takes the people away.
The final sentence merely restates the command as a mouth-opening move. The explanation feels flat.
The passage does not say Ezekiel is surprised by the taste.
Writing on both sides does not establish that the scroll has no empty space.
The passage does not say whether Ezekiel argues or stalls.
The stated reason does not establish that their refusal has nothing to do with Ezekiel at all.
Being sent to his own people does not establish that Ezekiel is personally known to them or is no stranger to them.
The explanation is flat and repeats the answer without adding insight.
The sound-system joke makes the glory of the LORD part of the joke.
The passage does not say the exiles are waiting for Ezekiel or that they are down a road.
Ezekiel ate the scroll; the passage does not say he carries it. The explanation also guesses at a reason for his bitterness and anger, which the text does not give.
The passage does not say Ezekiel gives no speech during the seven days. The explanation also guesses why he sat, though the text gives no reason.
